home.title: NVMe Monitor — External SSD temperature and SMART for Mac
home.description: See external NVMe SSD temperature and SMART health in your Mac menu bar. Monitor compatible drives, set local alerts, and read temperature in Shortcuts.
home.intro: See temperature and SMART health for your external NVMe drives, right in the Mac menu bar.
home.heroAlt: NVMe Monitor shows a connected external SSD, its composite and sensor temperatures, and SMART readings
home.temperatureBody: See the current reading in °C or °F while you work.
home.smartBody: Check drive wear, media errors and sensor readings.
home.alertsBody: Get notified when a drive overheats or reports a critical warning.
home.compatibilityHeading: Will it work with my SSD?
home.enclosureBody: The enclosure must expose NVMe SMART data to macOS.

support.title: NVMe Monitor Support and SSD Compatibility
support.description: Check external NVMe enclosure compatibility, troubleshoot missing SMART data, and contact NVMe Monitor support.
support.heading: NVMe Monitor Support
support.intro: Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened. Include your Mac model, macOS version, SSD model and enclosure model if they are relevant.
support.compatibilityBody: NVMe Monitor needs macOS 27 or later and an external SSD that macOS can see as native NVMe. Compatible Thunderbolt and USB4 enclosures can expose the controller over PCIe. Some enclosures hide SMART data even when Finder can access your files.
support.missing: My drive or its SMART data is missing
support.step1: Confirm the SSD appears as a physical drive in Disk Utility.
support.step2: Connect the enclosure directly with an appropriate Thunderbolt or USB4 cable, if supported.
support.step3: Choose Refresh in NVMe Monitor. If your manually selected drive has reconnected, select it again in Settings → Monitoring.
support.notificationsBody: Enable notifications in Settings → Alerts and allow them in macOS. In Settings → Monitoring, choose Celsius, Fahrenheit, or the system setting.
support.diagnosticsBody: In Settings → Support & Privacy, you can preview or clear local MetricKit reports. Choose Attach MetricKit Diagnostics if you wish to share a report. Enter the support address in your email draft and review the message and attachment before sending.

privacy.title: NVMe Monitor Privacy Policy
privacy.description: Learn what NVMe Monitor reads locally and how optional diagnostics, support email and privacy choices work.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: NVMe Monitor processes external SSD readings on your Mac. It does not automatically send them to the publisher or third parties.
privacy.readingsBody: The app reads device details such as the model, connection type, capacity and current macOS disk identifier, plus SMART temperatures, warnings, errors and usage counters. It does not open drive files, store serial numbers or retain a history of SMART readings. Preferences, the warning state and a boot-session identifier are stored locally to restore your choices, avoid duplicate warnings and distinguish drive connections.
privacy.diagnosticsBody: macOS may provide performance reports and technical diagnostics such as crash or hang traces. The app does not add drive readings, identifiers or preferences. It keeps up to five reports from the last seven days locally. Use Settings → Support & Privacy to preview or delete them. Temporary attachment copies are cleared on subsequent launches or when you delete reports. Copies saved or sent by your mail app are managed separately.
privacy.emailBody: Write Email opens an editable draft with an empty recipient field and the app and macOS versions. The optional diagnostics JSON is included only if you select it. Review or remove it before sending. The app does not send the email or upload reports. If your mail app cannot attach the file, you can attach the local copy yourself. The publisher uses what you choose to share to respond and investigate the issue.
privacy.notificationsBody: If you allow notifications, macOS delivers them and manages their visibility. They may show the drive model and the relevant reading or warning. Launch at login is optional and macOS manages the registration.
privacy.choicesBody: The app requires no account and uses no advertising, tracking or analytics. It does not sell your data. Settings and warning state stay local until updated or removed. Use macOS to revoke notification permission, clear delivered alerts or remove the login item. To remove saved settings and warning state, remove local app data when uninstalling.
privacy.websiteBody: Cloudflare hosts this site and processes connection information to serve and protect it. The site uses no advertising or analytics scripts. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards support email to the publisher’s Gmail inbox. The providers process messages and attachments to deliver and store them.
privacy.contact: Contact us with privacy questions or to request deletion of information you shared by email.
privacy.localPreferences: The site saves your appearance and temperature-unit preferences in your browser.
